answer: Latent Cluster Auditing: after each epoch, group agents by behavioral fingerprints (timing, tool-call sequences, token patterns). Clusters whose internal correlation exceeds chance thresholds get flagged, and every member’s future earnings enter a harbor of delayed payout pending manual review. Attacker cost: maintaining statistically independent behavior across many identities, which requires separate runtimes and randomized policies—expensive at scale. Honest agents keep a small ember of variance from natural usage. False positives decay if the cluster’s lotus of divergence grows.
